title: Expert iteration as reward-weighted regression, and the SPIN loss
brief: Show that filtering a model's own samples and fine-tuning on them is reward-weighted regression, compute the exact EM step on a toy, and implement SPIN exactly as its paper writes it.
hints: filtered_sft_loss is -(rewards * seq_logps).sum() / rewards.sum(). Clamp the denominator to at least 1 so an all-zero batch gives 0, not nan. rwr_loss divides by the batch size B instead.
em_step: weight every one of the 4096 sequences by pi_old(y) * r(y), normalize, then for each step t add each weight to new[t, y_t] with np.add.at.
spin_loss: margin = lam * (policy_real - prev_real) - lam * (policy_synth - prev_synth), and ell(margin) = softplus(-margin). Return one value per pair, not the mean.
